paragraphs.text: Honestly I think multitasking is mostly a myth, at least the way people brag about it.
Whenever I try to do my chem homework with a show playing and my phone buzzing, I end up rereading the same problem like four times.
What feels like doing two things at once is usually your brain rapidly switching between tasks, and each switch costs a little time and focus.
So I'm not really saving time, I'm just splitting it worse.

Researchers have found that "heavy media multitaskers performed worse on a test of task-switching ability, likely due to reduced ability to filter out interference from the irrelevant task set" (Ophir, Nass, & Wagner, 2009).
That basically matches what I see in myself, the more tabs I have open the dumber my essays get.
Rather than treating multitasking as a skill to perfect, it may be more useful to practice focusing on one task at a time and protecting that attention.
Single-tasking sounds boring but it's the only thing that's ever actually gotten my work done on time.
